transcript.text: The sides of our new fridge freezer get really warm, almost hot, especially near the front edge. Is that a fire risk? It's in an alcove between two units.

No, warm sides are not normally a fire risk. Modern fridge-freezers often have their condenser coils built into the side panels to save space and improve efficiency; as the compressor works to cool the inside, it pumps heat out through these sides, which can feel quite hot. However, because yours is in an alcove, we need to make sure there is enough airflow. If the unit is pushed too tight against the sides or back, the heat gets trapped and could cause the appliance to overheat or use excessive energy. Please check if there is at least a 5cm gap around the sides and back for ventilation. Also, listen to see if the compressor (the motor hum you hear from the back) runs constantly without ever switching off, even after it has been running for a day.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
The gap is only about 1cm each side, with a cupboard above that has a few cm gap. No burning smell or scorching, and nothing has tripped. Should I be worried about that gap?

Yes, 1cm is too tight. Most manufacturers require at least 5cm of clear space around the sides and back to allow heat to escape safely; with only 1cm, the heat gets trapped against your units, which can cause the appliance to overheat, use excessive energy, or potentially shorten its lifespan. To give you the exact clearance specs for your specific unit and check if there are any model-specific issues, could you please provide the brand and full model number? It is usually on a sticker inside the fridge, often on a side wall near the salad drawer.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It's a Hotpoint, model H7X 93T SK. I have the manual too, if that helps.

With only 1cm gaps, the heat generated by the cooling system is being trapped against your cabinetry. This forces the compressor to work much harder than necessary to dissipate that heat, which explains why the sides feel very hot and increases energy usage. While it isn't an immediate fire risk given no burning smell or tripping, it can damage the appliance over time. Please pull the fridge-freezer out from the alcove so there is at least 5cm of clear space on both sides and the back. This allows heat to escape safely. Once you have done this, leave it running for a few hours and check if the sides remain excessively hot or if they cool down slightly.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

I'd rather not pull it out, we've just had new flooring laid and I'm worried about scratching it. Is there anything else I can do without moving it? The manual says to leave space but I didn't check exactly how much.

You don't need to move it if you can create a small gap using spacers. Place rigid objects (like folded cardboard or wooden blocks) between the sides of the fridge and your cupboard walls to force at least 2–3cm of space. This allows air to circulate without risking scratches on your new floor. If you cannot achieve this gap, the heat will continue to build up; in that case, I would recommend contacting a professional appliance technician to inspect the unit's cooling performance and ensure it isn't overheating due to the installation constraints.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
Ok, I can try spacers, but with only about 1cm each side, how would I get 2-3cm without moving it? Should I just get an engineer in instead?

To get 2-3cm without moving the whole fridge, you can slide thin, rigid spacers (like wooden shims or folded card) into the gap at the top and bottom corners where the side meets the cupboard wall. This pushes the unit out slightly without dragging it across the floor. If you cannot achieve this gap safely, the appliance will continue to overheat and use excessive energy. In that case, you would need to either reposition the unit or consult a fitter about modifying the alcove, rather than calling an appliance repair engineer.

Sorry, I'm confused. You said fitter or repositioning, but not an engineer? I can't see how to get 2-3cm without moving it. Is it actually safe to keep using it as it is for now? It's cooling fine, 4C and -18C.

Yes, it is safe to keep using it as it is for now. Because there is no burning smell, tripping, or scorching marks, there is no immediate fire risk. However, because it is in a tight alcove with only 1cm gaps, the appliance has to work harder than necessary to get rid of that heat. This won't cause a fire, but it will use more electricity and may shorten the life of the compressor over time. Since you cannot move it without risking your new floor, try wedging thin spacers (like folded card or wood) into the top and bottom corners of the side gaps to push it out slightly. If that is not possible, just accept that it will run a bit hotter and use more power, but it will remain safe.
